newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek leftist group says it shot shipowner.
newsitem.headline: Greek leftist group says it shot shipowner.

text.p: The November 17 urban guerrilla group on Friday claimed responsibility for the assassination on Wednesday of Greek shipowner Constantine Peratikos and said he had been a target since 1995.

In an eight-page letter sent to the Eleftherotypia newspaper the group accused Greek politicians, shipowners and businessmen of "stealing state property" and described privatisation of state firms as "major scandals."
Peratikos, 42, was ambushed on Wednesday afternoon in Piraeus, Greece's main port near Athens, as he was heading for a garage to get his car.

Police said ballistic tests of the bullets found at the site showed the pistol was the same used by November 17 in eleven attacks since it emerged in 1975. Hospital officials said Peratikos was shot seven times.

The Peratikos Group, owned by one of Greece's major shipping families, took over the troubled Elefsis Shipyards in the early 1990s. But the Group was unable to complete payments it had agreed with the Greek government and the shipyards have since reverted to state hands.

"The attack was planned for June 1995 when Elefsis Shipyards were owned by Peratikos. His sudden decision to close down the yard in August 1995 and suspend his business operations in Greece made (the attack) impossible. There was another attempt (to shoot him) in 1996 without success," the group said.
Peratikos left Greece in late 1995 and returned some time later.
"The Greek people will not allow the shipowners to cheat them and steal from them billions while poor citizens are sent to jail for owing small sums to the state," the group's statement added.

November 17, which has killed 21 Greeks, Americans and Turks since emerging in 1975, also made reference to a crisis between Greece and Turkey over rights of an uninhabited Aegean Sea islet in January 1996 which ended with U.S. mediation.
It said Prime Minister Costas Simitis had no choice but to accept pressure by Washington and start a dialogue with Turkey over mineral and territorial rights in the Aegean.
Peratikos' shooting may have signalled the re-emergence of the group, which had been dormant since a bungled rocket attack on the U.S. embassy in January 1996.

Police found .45 calibre shells at the site of the shooting. November 17 uses a trademark .45 calibre pistol as a signature in many of its attacks. It is also versed in remote-controlled bombs and rockets.
November 17's previous fatal attack was against Turkish embassy Counsellor Omer Haluk Sipahioglu, who was shot by a three-man hit squad outside his home in June 1994.
The group named itself after the day in 1973 when Greece's then-ruling military junta used tanks to put down a student uprising.
